item.title: Version 3.4.0
item.description:
This release fixes a ton of little desync bugs between the editor and sim which caused odd visual glitches

New

  • Thicker lines in exported images (#127). Exports at 2x, 4x and 6x drew lines one pixel wide which made them super thin.
  • Adjustable hit zones. Preferences has Pin Hit Zone and Wire Hit Zone, so you can set how close the mouse has to be to start a wire or grab one.
  • Desktop shortcut from the Windows installer. The last page of the installer has a Create a Desktop shortcut box, and a Run CedarLogic box.
  • Cmd-drag (Ctrl-drag on Windows and Linux) from a wire to a pin connects them. It used to draw the green line and then do nothing.

Fixes

Gates showing the wrong value

  • Undoing the deletion of a gate brought it back without its inverted pins.
  • Undoing a rotation or any parameter change could disconnect the gate from its wires inside the simulator, leaving it stuck at unknown. It also rewound live values such as a counter's count.
  • Moving a pin onto a different wire left the old wire stuck at its last value.
  • Opening a file no longer clocks every flip-flop whose clock input is already high. A saved counter used to count up by one each time it was opened.
  • A disabled tri-state buffer or ROM added to a running circuit no longer makes its bus read unknown once nothing else is driving it.
  • Large circuits (thousands of gates) no longer lose signals on busy steps.
  • Registers and LED displays show their digits in blue again when the value they latched was never known.
  • The 16-bit counter counts to 65535 and wraps, instead of sitting on 0 for an extra clock.

Losing work

  • Answering Yes to "save first?" and then cancelling the save dialog no longer closes the window or clears the circuit anyway, and no longer deletes the crash-recovery copy with it.
  • Saving as V1 or V2 is now safe against a full disk or a crash part way through, like V3 already was.
  • A RAM or ROM keeps its contents through delete and undo, and through copy and paste.
  • Recovering two crashed sessions in one launch no longer throws the first one away.
  • A pin that two wires claimed could switch to the other wire after the file was reopened. Saved files now record only the wire actually on the pin.
  • Opening a V1 or V2 file keeps spaces at the ends of labels, so named links such as A and A stay separate.
  • Exporting to V1 or V2 warns when a label contains #, which older CedarLogic cuts off.

Editing

  • A gate dropped after dragging keeps the wire shape shown during the drag, instead of the wire jumping.
  • Clicking just beside a highlighted wire grabs it, instead of doing nothing and clearing the selection.
  • Panning with the middle button, or right-clicking, while dragging no longer drops what you were dragging. Escape during a wire drag puts the wire back.
  • Straightening a wire by dragging no longer makes it vanish while still connected.
  • Undoing the deletion of a gate whose wire looped back to itself restores the wire whole.
  • Right-clicking a RAM's data pin removes the wire instead of leaving one end dangling.
  • Rotating with R can be undone, and a second paste while the first is still on the cursor is ignored instead of losing the first.
  • Undoing a paste that made no gates no longer crashes.
  • A file with two gates sharing an id says so instead of quietly losing one.
  • File > New releases the lock on the file it closed.
  • Oscilloscope layouts saved on Windows open on macOS and Linux.

Crashes

  • Deleting a gate no longer crashes after its pins have overlapped another gate's.
  • The canvas no longer crashes when its window is tiled on macOS.

Internal

  • New tests drive a NOR state machine through thousands of clock cycles, and check each library gate's parameters against the simulator.
  • Simpler message handling between the editor and the simulator thread, and a fix for a step that could start while another was still running.
  • Headless --render loads its file once.
